title: Support Worker
company: Nottingham Community Housing Association Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Support Worker

Location: Nottingham

Salary: 24,871 - 25,371 per annum

Our client believes everyone deserves the opportunity to live a fulfilling, independent life. We're looking for compassionate, resilient and motivated Support Workers to join our Supported Living and Community Outreach services, supporting people with learning disabilities, autism, mental health conditions, physical disabilities and other complex needs to achieve their goals and live well.

About the role

As a Support Worker, you'll work closely with our customers to provide person-centred, trauma-informed support that promotes independence, choice and wellbeing. You'll help people develop life skills, maintain their tenancies, access education, employment and leisure activities, and build meaningful connections within their communities.

No two days are the same. You could be supporting someone to attend an appointment, helping with daily living tasks, administering medication, completing support plans, or encouraging an individual to achieve a personal goal that matters to them.

Key responsibilities
- Providing tailored support based on individual needs, strengths and aspirations.
- Working with customers to develop and review support plans and risk assessments.
- Supporting people with daily living activities, personal care, health and wellbeing.
- Helping individuals access work, training, education and community opportunities.
- Building positive relationships with customers, families and partner agencies.
- Safely administering and recording medication.
- Maintaining accurate records using our clients systems.

About you

We're looking for someone who:
- Has a genuine passion for supporting people and making a positive difference.
- Understands the needs and challenges faced by vulnerable adults.
- Can communicate clearly, professionally and compassionately.
- Is comfortable using basic IT systems, including emails and record-keeping.
- Can remain calm and resilient in challenging situations.
- Understands the importance of professional boundaries and confidentiality.

Previous experience in care and support is welcomed, but your willingness to learn, your values and your commitment is just as important to helping others achieve independence and life opportunities.

Additional Information
- This role is based within our Supported Living and Community Outreach services and may require working across different settings and client groups.
- The role operates on a rota basis and includes weekend, bank holiday, night-time and sleep-in duties where required.
- This role is subject to an Enhanced DBS check, including a barred list check.
- Please note that we are not offering visa sponsorship

As an Equal Opportunities and Disability Confident Employer, our client welcomes applications from all suitably qualified candidates including those from Black, Asian and minority ethnic groups and disabled candidates. As part of our LGBT + Allies Programme, we also welcome applications from members of the LGBT + community and encourage inclusivity in the workplace.

Closing date: 10th November 2026

Shortlist date: 11th November 2026

Interview date: TBC

title: Severe and Multiple Disadvantage (SMD) Support Worker
description:
Severe and Multiple Disadvantage (SMD) Support Worker

Location: South Nottinghamshire County (Ashfield, Broxtowe, Gedling, Rushcliffe & Mansfield)
Hours: 30 hours per week over 4 days
Salary: Juno Scale Point 17
Contract: Fixed Term until March 2027

Make a Real Difference to Women's Lives

At Juno Women's Aid, we believe every woman deserves the opportunity to live safely, recover from trauma and build the future she wants. We are looking for a passionate, compassionate and highly motivated SMD Support Worker to join our team and support women experiencing domestic abuse alongside severe and multiple disadvantage.

This is a rewarding opportunity to work directly with women facing complex challenges such as homelessness, mental ill-health, substance use and involvement with the criminal justice system. You will provide specialist, trauma-informed support that empowers women to improve their safety, wellbeing and independence.

About the Role

As an SMD Support Worker, you will:
- Build trusting relationships with women experiencing domestic abuse and multiple disadvantage.
- Provide tailored emotional and practical support to help women achieve their goals.
- Complete risk assessments, safety planning and support plans.
- Advocate on behalf of survivors and help them navigate complex systems.
- Support access to accommodation, healthcare, substance misuse services, mental health support, legal advice and other specialist services.
- Attend and contribute to multi-agency meetings, including MARAC and other partnership forums.
- Work collaboratively with housing providers, social care, safeguarding services and community partners.
- Promote survivor voice, empowerment and recovery.

What We're Looking For

We would love to hear from you if you have:
- Experience supporting vulnerable adults with complex needs.
- Experience working with survivors of domestic abuse, gender-based violence or related support services.
- A good understanding of trauma-informed and survivor-centred practice.
- Knowledge of safeguarding adults and children.
- Strong advocacy, communication and partnership-working skills.
- Experience managing a caseload and delivering person-centred support.
- The ability to work independently while remaining a supportive team member.

Why Join Juno Women's Aid?

At Juno, you'll become part of a dedicated team committed to supporting women and children across Nottinghamshire. We offer:
- The opportunity to make a genuine difference to women's lives every day.
- A supportive and inclusive working environment.
- Ongoing training and professional development opportunities.
- A values-led organisation committed to equality, empowerment and social justice.
- The chance to help shape and develop innovative services for women experiencing multiple disadvantage.

Essential Requirements
- Enhanced DBS clearance.
- Full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle insured for business use.
- Ability to travel across Nottinghamshire.
- Commitment to Juno Women's Aid values and survivor-centred practice.

Occupational Requirement

This post is open to women only under Schedule 9, Part 1 of the Equality Act 2010 due to the nature of the service and client group.

Join our specialist team supporting women to achieve safety, recovery and independence today.

title: Care Assistant - Nights
company: Hamberley Care Management Limited - Company - Permanent
description:
Be all you can be with Hamberley
At Hamberley, we believe that our residents deserve something 'Extra Special, Every Day' and we're recruiting for a Care Assistant to help us achieve our goals.
At Edwalton Manor, our Care Assistants are called Homemakers. More than support workers, care assistants or healthcare assistants - they are carers and companions all in one. They have the time to get to know our residents and are trusted to give each person the care they need, in the way they like.
Joining us at Edwalton Manor, our luxury care home that provides residential, dementia, and nursing care for older people, you'll be part of a team that is genuinely passionate about the health and well-being of our residents.
Working Pattern: 12 hour shifts and working alternate weekends on a rota basis. (8pm - 8am)
We offer our Care Assistants - our Homemakers:
- Competitive salary and benefits package
- 28 days holiday (inclusive of Bank Holidays)
- Quality bonus scheme linked to CQC rating
- Workplace pension
- A supportive and collaborative working environment
- Opportunities for professional development and training
- Access to high street discounts via our mobile friendly HapiApp benefits platform
- Free onsite parking available
- Unlimited Refer a Friend Bonus - up to £750 per referral - t&cs apply
- Employee Assistance Programme, occupational health support and wellbeing services

Be different - be a Homemaker
Be at the heart of our award winning homemaker care mode. A Homemaker is a unique caring role for a unique person, where you can care with a difference.
- A varied role where no two days are the same. Homemakers, our name for care assistants, care for individual people in the way a family member might care for someone in their home. We don't do timetabled task-based care - we care for each individual in the way that works best for them. Whether that's administering medication, helping make someone's bed, arranging a family meal with their loved ones or taking them to the beauty salon, you'll always be doing something different. Our Homemakers focus on the tiny details that make our residents unique, and tailor care to each and every individual.
- A chance to make a real difference to our residents' lives. Often healthcare assistants, care assistants and domiciliary care assistants find they don't get to spend enough time with the people they care for to make a real difference. Not at Hamberley. As a Homemaker you have fewer people to care for, but you spend more time with them. It's a more satisfying and fulfilling role that is better for our residents. That's why the model has won awards.
- Excellent opportunities for learning and development. We will support you with all the training you need, including NVQ qualifications and further clinical training if you want to specialise in areas like dementia and nutrition.
- Supportive team environment. Being kind and supportive to each other is key to our ability to show kindness and companionship to our residents. We truly believe this across all parts of our organisation. It's just one of the reasons that, when people join us, they stay with us.

Could you be part of our team?
We provide full training and induction, so we're more interested in you as a person than your specific care experience.
You may have experience as a healthcare assistant, care assistant, carer, home care assistant or domiciliary care assistant and are looking for a different approach, a nicer work environment and a more satisfying role.
If you have no work experience in care but are interested in helping people live happy lives, we'll guide you to a fantastic care assistant career at Hamberley.
What is important is that you have passion, empathy and dedication to help our residents live their lives to the fullest. We will support you with everything else!
If this sounds like you and you're looking for a fulfilling role that makes a genuine impact in the lives of others, this rewarding career is for you.
Join us at Nottingham's most stunning care home
Edwalton Manor, is a luxurious care home in Nottingham, part of the award-winning Hamberley Care Homes - offering luxury care homes in beautiful locations throughout the UK. Residents live in spacious, stylish ensuite rooms, and enjoy beautifully furnished shared spaces and landscaped gardens. From the deluxe picture house - where we screen classic films - to the on-site luxury spa - offering hairdressing, manicures and relaxing therapies - everything has been designed and finished with the care and attention you would expect from a 5-star hotel.
Hamberley People
We respect and value our residents and each other. At Hamberley Care Homes, we believe in the importance of what we do and why we do it. Creative and empowered, our people see every day as an opportunity for growth and development. We make ideas happen. Together we can achieve anything. Be part of it!

title: Children'S Residential Support Worker
company: Sal Integrated Care Limited, Mambaridge Lodge - Agency - Permanent
description:
Residential Children's Home Support Worker

Organisation: Sal Integrated Care Ltd
Residential Home: Mambaridge Lodge
Location: Worksop, Nottinghamshire
Job Title: Residential Children's Home Support Worker
Salary: £26,325 to £27,300 per annum or £13.50 £14.00 per hour, depending on experience and qualifications
Contract: Full-time
Working Hours: Rota-based, including evenings, weekends, bank holidays and sleep-in duties where required.
Responsible to: Registered Manager / Deputy Manager

1. About Mambaridge Lodge

Mambaridge Lodge is a four-bedded children's residential home operated by Sal Integrated Care Ltd. The home provides a safe, nurturing and supportive environment for children and young people aged 8 17 who may have experienced adverse childhood experiences, trauma, emotional and behavioural difficulties, family breakdown or other challenges in their lives.

Our approach is child-centred, therapeutic and relationship-based. We are committed to providing high-quality care that promotes children's safety, emotional well-being, independence, personal development and positive outcomes.

We are looking for compassionate, committed and enthusiastic individuals who share our commitment to making a positive difference in the lives of children and young people.

2. Purpose of the Role

The Residential Children's Home Support Worker will provide day-to-day care, support and guidance to children and young people living at Mambaridge Lodge.

The successful candidate will help create a safe, stable and homely environment where children feel valued, respected, listened to and supported. They will build positive and trusting relationships with children, promote their independence and encourage them to develop the skills and confidence needed to achieve their full potential.

3. Main Duties and Responsibilities

Care and Support

Provide consistent, compassionate and individualised care to children and young people.

Develop positive, trusting and professional relationships with children.

Support children with their daily routines, personal care, hygiene and independent living skills.

Encourage children to participate in educational, recreational, social and community activities.

Promote children's self-esteem, confidence, independence and personal development.

Support children to maintain appropriate relationships with family members and significant others, in accordance with their care plans.

Safeguarding and Protection

Promote and safeguard the welfare of all children and young people living at the home.

Maintain a good understanding of safeguarding procedures, child protection and contextual safeguarding.

Identify, recognise and respond appropriately to signs of abuse, neglect, exploitation, bullying, radicalisation and other safeguarding concerns.

Report and record incidents, concerns and significant events promptly in accordance with organisational policies.

Follow individual risk assessments, behaviour management plans and placement plans.

Maintain appropriate professional boundaries and promote children's rights, dignity and privacy.

Therapeutic and Behavioural Support

Support children who may experience emotional distress, trauma and behavioural difficulties.

Apply a therapeutic, trauma-informed and relationship-based approach to care.

Demonstrate patience, empathy, curiosity and understanding when responding to challenging situations.

Promote positive behaviour through encouragement, positive reinforcement and consistent boundaries.

Use de-escalation and conflict-resolution techniques to manage challenging situations safely.

Support children to understand and regulate their emotions and develop positive coping strategies.

Apply the organisation's therapeutic approach, including PACE (Playfulness, Acceptance, Curiosity and Empathy), where appropriate.

Household and Daily Responsibilities

Assist with the preparation of meals and encourage healthy eating.

Support children to maintain a clean, safe and welcoming living environment.

Participate in household activities, including shopping, cooking and recreational activities.

Administer medication in accordance with prescribed procedures, following appropriate training and authorisation.

Maintain accurate daily records, handovers and other relevant documentation.

Participate in team meetings, supervision, training and professional development.

Teamwork and Professional Development

Work collaboratively with colleagues, managers, social workers, families and other professionals.

Follow organisational policies, procedures, the home's Statement of Purpose and relevant regulatory requirements.

Attend mandatory and specialist training as required.

Participate in regular supervision, reflective practice and performance reviews.

Contribute to the development and continuous improvement of the home's care practices.

4. Qualifications and Experience

Essential:

A genuine commitment to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people.

Good communication and interpersonal skills.

Ability to work effectively as part of a team and independently when required.

A caring, patient, resilient and responsible attitude.

Ability to maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality.

Willingness to undertake relevant training and professional development.

Ability to work flexible shifts, including evenings, weekends and bank holidays.

Desirable:

Level 3 Diploma in Residential Childcare or an equivalent recognised qualification

Previous experience working with children and young people, particularly in residential childcare, social care, education or a related setting

Knowledge of safeguarding, child development, trauma-informed care and positive behaviour support

Experience supporting children with emotional and behavioural difficulties - A full, valid UK driving licence.

Training and Qualifications:

Candidates who do not currently hold a Level 3 Diploma in Residential Childcare will be considered,

provided they demonstrate the right attitude, commitment and willingness to undertake the qualification within the required regulatory timescales.

Sal Integrated Care Ltd will support successful candidates to access appropriate training and development opportunities.

5. Personal Attributes and Skills

The successful candidate should demonstrate:

Compassion-

empathy and a genuine interest in improving children's lives

Patience, emotional resilience and the ability to remain calm under pressure
